headline: Banco Central do Brasil Holds Selic Rate at 13.75%, Pausing Cut Cycle
summary: Brazil's monetary policy committee Copom maintained the benchmark Selic rate at 13.75%, halting a sequence of five consecutive cuts. Commercial banks adjusted mortgage rates upward following fiscal uncertainty concerns.
why: Banco Central do Brasil sets benchmark interest rates for Latin America's largest economy. Pausing rate cuts directly impacts commercial mortgage lending rates, bond yields, and domestic equity valuations.

impacts.name: Brazil Selic Rate
impacts.why: Holding the Selic at 13.75% maintains elevated borrowing costs across commercial credit markets.
